Haemon argued from reason, the people's view and his father's reputation, but the Chorus explains his defiance as the work of Love, who kindled this feud of kinsman with kin. Love resistless in fight, all yield at a glance of thine eye,
Love who pillowed all night on a maiden’s cheek dost lie,
Over the upland folds thou roam’st, and the trackless sea.
Love the gods captive holds. Shall mortals not yield to thee?
Mad are thy subjects all, and even the wisest heart
Straight to folly will fall, at a touch of thy poisoned dart.

Thus hurried down

weDoAnswers: Eros (Love) was a powerful god in Greek belief; the elders trace the quarrel they have just seen to Love. Read closely: “Lo I myself am borne aside, From Justice, as I view this bride.” (Chorus, lines 747–748).
analysis.weDoWords: “Borne aside” and “Justice” stand out in lines 747–748. The elders admit that pity is pulling them away from the strict justice they owe the king, so even they are moved by Antigone’s fate. “Borne aside, / From Justice, as I view this bride” makes the pull visible and personal.

segments.script:
Today's words: resistless — (poetic) impossible to resist; trackless — having no path or trail; winsome — charming in a sweet or appealing way; yearning — a deep longing; invincible — impossible to defeat; bower — a leafy shelter or inner chamber.

Eros (Love) was a powerful god in Greek belief; the elders trace the quarrel to Love they have just seen. The elders reduce Haemon's principled argument to passion, a judgment the play does not fully support. Imagery: Love is given eyes, a pillow and a roaming path over folds and sea, so an abstract power becomes a figure that touches bodies and places. Theme: The elders blame the quarrel on Love’s irresistible force, reducing Haemon’s argument about the State to passion alone. Tone / mood: The ode is half hymn and half confession: the Chorus admits it is “borne aside, From Justice” as it looks at the bride. Watch for burial and the unburied body: The “bride” they pity is walking toward a tomb, so the love-song is already a burial song in disguise.
